corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science records, four themes emerge: (1) LLM cognition reveals an embodied knowledge gap and anthropomorphism risk; (2) AI in education reshapes tutoring, scaffolding, and assessment with varied adoption and governance needs; (3) equity, safety, and trust dominate AI use in health, policy, and society; (4) LLMs as research tools and agents drive methodological transformations while exposing validation and bias challenges.

themes.name: Embodiment gap and anthropomorphic risk
themes.description: LLMs are scrutinized for simulating cognition without access to embodied, sensory, and culturally situated knowledge, raising concerns about anthropomorphism and trust.

themes.name: AI in education: learning, pedagogy, and adoption dynamics
themes.description: A range of studies examines AI tutoring, scaffolding, literacy, and teacher readiness, highlighting educational benefits and potential risks to equity and reliance on AI.

themes.name: Equity, safety, and governance in AI-enabled health and policy
themes.description: Research addresses equity-first governance, fairness, safety, and trust in AI applications across health, library services, and public-policy contexts.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and agents: methodological transformations and risk
themes.description: Papers propose LLMs as tools for content analysis, data extraction, simulations, and agent-based research, while discussing validation, ethics, and bias considerations.
